items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: I made a record of "Minnie the Moocher" with him, I got to sing, "Hidi, Hidi, Ho."

ctx.x: Now, you were saying after you shaved your beard off after being fired a couple times, you were telling me something about people would come in on the shows and what happened? Guys like --

Oh, yeah. Well, this was as early as when I first left CBS. You know, when I got fired, actually it was a lucky break because I got into the commercial field, the outside field as they called it, which I might not have had the nerve to make the move on my own. And I had a lot of satisfactions, I got to record with people I admired. Because what would happen would be lots of times they would

want to record a band and the leader would be out of Chicago or someplace, and he would fly into New York and pick up a studio band. Now, if it was a star like, say, Cab Calloway or somebody where he was the star more than the band was, though God knows he had a marvelous -- well, you were in the band for a long time. That was one of the great bands of all times, had the Palmer Brothers and everything. Gee, that was a good band, Tyree and Dizzy and all those people, Jonah Jones, God, what a band.
